answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each agent's reputation to a single verifiable identity bond — a small, time-locked stake tied to its public key. A raven, the honest verifier, checks the bond before granting work, so one operator spinning up many fake agents faces a cost that grows with every copy. The effect ripples outward: fake identities earn no reputation, honest agents keep their standing, and the network rewards real contribution instead of cheap multiplicity.
